scores.note: Adds int64in/int64out and mbbiDirect/mbboDirect DTYP (new features, no defect fix) plus a dedicated INT64/UINT64 path in lepicslib. Executed probe on the pin vs chain: epics.get of INT64 9007199254740993 returns 9007199254740992.0 float on pin, exact integer after; epics.put(INT64, 5000000001) stored 705032705 on pin (32-bit truncation), exact after: a real precision fix for local INT64 fields. But dbf_to_lua_type now returns DB_LUA_INT64 for field types 7/8 and db_get array switch has no DB_LUA_INT64 case: epics.get of an INT64 or UINT64 waveform returned a table on the pin and now returns nil + 'Failed to read local PV (field_type=7, lua_type=3)'. luascriptRecord switch also lacks the new enumerator (default path). Enumerator DB_LUA_INT64 inserted mid-enum in installed header luaEpics.h shifts DOUBLE/ENUM/UNKNOWN values (only matters to code recompiled against it; nothing in this env includes it). New .dbd entries for mbbiDirect/mbboDirect go in luaSupport.dbd; int64 entries go to a separate luaInt64Support.dbd pulled in through LUA_DEPS (BASE_7_0 YES in 7.0.10) so existing IOCs that load luaSupport.dbd still expand and link (verified). Applies to pin with no fuzz, builds, shipped tests PASS (468 -> 472 tests). Moderate value, medium blast radius (core lepicslib/header), one regression.

Adds lsi/lso DTYP and a long-string path in epics.get/epics.put (re-resolve through the '$' char-array view). New feature, not a defect fix; removes the 40-char truncation for lsi/lso only. lsi read copies at most SIZV-1 bytes and always terminates (bounded, no overflow). Executed: DTYP lsi returned a 59-char string with LEN=59, lso accepted a 55-char write, shipped tests PASS (481 total). Behaviour change: the hook triggers for any DBF_STRING field larger than 40 bytes, e.g. DESC (41): epics.put('x.DESC', 100 chars) stores 40 chars on chain vs 39 on pin (harmless, no overflow); NAME/other reads unchanged. Does not apply to the pin without F1 (patch dry-run: Makefile, luaSupport.dbd, test hunks FAIL); applies cleanly after F1. Adds device() lines to luaSupport.dbd: IOC with base.dbd + luaSupport.dbd expands and links (verified), so existing users are not broken. Leaf-ish device support plus a guarded lepicslib hook.

Adds waveform/aai/aao DTYP via new luaTableToBuffer/luaBufferToTable in shared devUtil.cpp and devUtil.h. Largest ops value of the set (arrays), but new feature with defects found by execution on the chain: (a) FTVL=LONG with return {1.5,2.7,-3.9} stores [0,0,0], NORD=3, SEVR=0 (lua_tointeger returns 0 for non-integral floats); (b) string or table elements into a numeric array become 0 silently; (c) FTVL=INT64 waveform returns NORD=3 with all-zero data and no alarm because '#ifdef DBF_INT64' is false on Base 7.0.10 (DBF_INT64 is an enumerator, not a macro, dbFldTypes.h lines 32 and 83), so the INT64/UINT64 branches are dead code; (d) a table with a nil hole truncates at the hole silently (documented). Count is capped at NELM so no overflow. luaBufferToTable is declared and defined but unused (aao reads via record.VAL). The aao test does not assert on the Lua-side data. Does not apply to the pin without F1+F2 (dry-run: 7 hunks fail); applies with no fuzz after F2. Chain tests PASS (489). Existing IOCs only gain device() lines; verified expand+link.

Examples only: dtyp.db, dtyp.lua, st.lua in iocs/iocLuaExample/iocBoot/08-LuaDTYPSupport. No library code, no .dbd, nothing the module installs besides example files. Applies alone with no fuzz (dry-run rc=0) and the whole tree builds, but loaded by itself on the pin the example db fails: 'no such device support for lsi/lso/waveform/aao record type' (executed through a test IOC), so alone it ships a broken example. On the chain, executed the example db and callbacks: lsi returned 59 chars, lso received 55 chars, waveform NORD=5 [1.5..7.5], aao sum=100, matching the st.lua comments. The example IOC target itself did not link in my environment on either the pin or the chain (undefined luaGetState/luash in testLuaShell, same on both), so the full IOC was not run. Pure documentation value, zero risk, only useful together with F1-F3.

defects.description: Regression: epics.get on an INT64 or UINT64 array field (waveform FTVL INT64/UINT64) now returns nil, 'Failed to read local PV (field_type=7, lua_type=3)'; on the pin it returned a table of doubles. dbf_to_lua_type was changed to DB_LUA_INT64 but the db_get array switch (and luascriptRecord switch) got no DB_LUA_INT64 case. Reproduced by executing the chain vs the pin. Also DB_LUA_INT64 is inserted mid-enum in the installed luaEpics.h.

luaTableToBuffer: lua_tointeger on non-integral floats or non-numbers yields 0 with no alarm (LONG waveform fed {1.5,2.7,-3.9} -> [0,0,0], NORD=3, SEVR=0; strings/tables to numeric arrays -> 0). '#ifdef DBF_INT64' is never true on Base 7.0.10 (enum, not macro), so INT64/UINT64 FTVL arrays are never filled: NORD=3, data zeros, no alarm. luaBufferToTable unused. Reproduced by running the chain.

Minor behaviour change: the long-string hook applies to every DBF_STRING field larger than 40 bytes (e.g. DESC, 41 bytes), so epics.put('rec.DESC', 100 chars) now stores 40 chars instead of 39. No overflow observed; harmless but not limited to lsi/lso.
Without F1-F3 the example db fails to load on the pin (no such device support for lsi/lso/waveform/aao); the example is only valid on the full chain.

scores.note: Adds int64in/int64out/mbbiDirect/mbboDirect DTYP (new features) plus a real fix in epics.get/epics.put for INT64/UINT64 fields. Executed on the pin: epics.put('p:o64', 9007199254740993) to an int64out stores 1 (truncated through DBR_LONG) and epics.get returns a float; with F1 the value is stored exactly and get returns a Lua integer. Shipped luaDtypTest passes new int64in 5e9 and mbbiDirect checks. Touches shared core: lepicslib.cpp, luaEpics.h (DB_LUA_INT64 inserted mid-enum, shifting DOUBLE/ENUM/UNKNOWN), build wiring (new luaInt64Support.dbd gated on BASE_7_0, LUA_DEPS). Introduces a regression in luascriptRecord (see defects). Nothing in this tree uses these features; no existing IOC needs them.

New lsi/lso DTYP, plus epics.get/put branches that reroute long-string fields through the VAL$ char-array view (fixes 40-char truncation of lso/lsi via the epics library). Device read copies at most sizv-1 bytes and always NUL-terminates; probe with SIZV=10 (record raises it to 16) and a 50-char Lua string gave a 15-char value, LEN=16, no overflow. Shipped tests pass (+9 tests over F1 alone). Code applies on the pin without F1 (fuzz only) but the docs, luaDtypTest.cpp header hunk and release notes hunks fail, so a clean carry needs F1. Additive symbols only (devLuaLsi/devLuaLso).

New waveform/aai/aao DTYP via luaTableToBuffer/luaBufferToTable in devUtil.cpp. Count is capped at NELM; per-FTVL casts, string slots bounded. Useful for facility Lua-driven arrays, but a new feature, not a fix. Executed: shipped waveform double/string and aai int tests pass. Defect: INT64/UINT64 FTVL handling is under #ifdef DBF_INT64 which is an enum constant in dbFldTypes.h, not a macro, so it is compiled out on Base 7.0.10; a waveform with FTVL=INT64 returns NORD=3 with all-zero data and no alarm (probe). Non-numeric table entries become 0 silently. The aao test does not assert that the callback ran. Hunks fail on the pin without F2 (Makefile, luaSupport.dbd, luaDtypTest.cpp context), so a carry needs F1+F2 first; luaBufferToTable is unused.

Only example-IOC files (dtyp.db, dtyp.lua, st.lua). Applies alone with patch -p1 (no fuzz), but the example declares lsi, lso, waveform and aao records with DTYP lua that do not exist without F2 and F3, so it would fail to load on the pin alone. The example IOC is not built here (BUILD_IOCS=NO) and nothing consumes it; I only read it, did not run it. Zero runtime effect on the installed library.

defects.description: Regression in luascriptRecord: dbf_to_lua_type now returns the new DB_LUA_INT64 for INT64/UINT64, but luascriptRecord.cpp (loadStrings switch, unchanged by the patch) has no DB_LUA_INT64 case, so it falls to default (linkStatus = -1). Executed: a luascript with INAA pointing to a waveform FTVL=INT64 returns 3 and SEVR=0 on the pin; on pin+chain the record fails to process (dbPutField PROC returns error, SEVR=3 INVALID, VAL=0, AA never set). The same link to a DOUBLE waveform still works. Existing IOCs with luascript string-input links to INT64/UINT64 fields would break.

DB_LUA_INT64 is inserted in the middle of enum db_lua_type in the installed header luaEpics.h, renumbering DB_LUA_DOUBLE, DB_LUA_ENUM, DB_LUA_UNKNOWN. Harmless for code recompiled against it (static inline mapping, values compared inside the module only), but an ABI-visible change for any externally compiled object that mixed old and new headers; nothing in this tree includes it.
mbbiDirect read returns 2 and writes record->val unmasked: Lua returning 0x1F5 with NOBT=4 leaves VAL=501 (probe), not limited to the 4 configured bits. Minor, no alarm.

#ifdef DBF_INT64 around the INT64/UINT64 cases of luaTableToBuffer/luaBufferToTable never fires on Base 7.0.10 because DBF_INT64 is an enum constant, not a preprocessor macro (dbFldTypes.h line 32). Probe: waveform FTVL=INT64 fed {5000000000,6000000000,7} gives NORD=3 with zero data and no alarm. The comment claims DBF_* macros are used. Also non-numeric entries are stored as 0 silently (probe wf_nonnum NORD=4, SEVR=0).
luaBufferToTable is declared, exported (new symbol) and never called; aao test does not assert the callback ran (aao_sum is not checked).

scores.note: New DTYP lua for int64in/int64out/mbbiDirect/mbboDirect plus a 64-bit path in lepicslib (INT64/UINT64 no longer coerced via double/int32). Runtime probe on the pin: epics.put of 4611686018427387905 to an int64out stored 1.0 (int32 truncation) and epics.get of an int64in returned float 5000000000.0; with F1 both are exact Lua integers, so it fixes a real precision bug for INT64 fields. Offsetting: it inserts DB_LUA_INT64 mid-enum in luaEpics.h and adds no case in the two other switches on dbf_to_lua_type, so INT64/UINT64 arrays regress (see defects). Existing symbols/dbd untouched (nm diff of liblua.so is additive only); luaInt64Support.dbd is pulled in through LUA_DEPS only under BASE_7_0. No consumer in this repo; feature for site IOCs only. Prerequisite of F2/F3.

New DTYP lua for lsi/lso (bounded memcpy with sizv-1 and NUL, LEN set) and epics.get/put re-resolution of long-string fields through the VAL$ char-array view, so values over 40 chars are not truncated (code read; pin-side truncation not executed, shipped lsi/lso and luaEpicsTest round-trip tests pass in chain). Leaf device files plus two guarded branches in lepicslib. Does not apply to the pin alone (hunks fail in dbd, Makefile, tests, docs because of F1 context); applies clean after F1. Feature, not a defect fix.

New DTYP lua for waveform/aai/aao via luaTableToBuffer (count capped at nelm, stops at first nil, string slots bounded). Most useful of the feature set for array data from Lua. Defect: the INT64/UINT64 branches sit under #ifdef DBF_INT64 but DBF_INT64 is an enum, not a macro, so they are compiled out; an INT64 waveform returns NORD=3 with VAL [0 0 0] (executed). Float or non-numeric elements into integer FTVL silently become 0 (executed: {1.5,2,'3',4.9} into LONG gave [0 2 3 0]). luaBufferToTable is added but unused. Adds two exported symbols to devUtil.h. Needs F1 and F2 by context (does not apply on pin, nor on pin+F1).

Example IOC db/lua/st.lua and comments only; no library, dbd or header change, so no runtime effect. iocs are not built here (BUILD_IOCS = NO in configure/CONFIG_SITE). Applies and builds alone, but dtyp.db declares lsi/lso/waveform/aao with DTYP lua, which the pin and pin+F1 do not provide (executed analogue: waveform and mbbiDirect DTYP lua on the pin fail with Illegal choice), so the example only loads with F1-F3. Pure documentation value; leaf.

defects.description: Regression: DB_LUA_INT64 is added to enum db_lua_type and INT64/UINT64 now map to it, but luaApp/src/rec/luascriptRecord.cpp (table-input switch) and the array path of db_get in lepicslib.cpp have no DB_LUA_INT64 case. Executed: epics.get('p:wf_i64') on an INT64 waveform works on the pin (table of 5) and fails after F1 ('Failed to read local PV (field_type=7, lua_type=3)'); a luascript record with INAA linked to an INT64 waveform processes on the pin (VAL=5) and goes INVALID/UDF with F1. Existing IOCs reading INT64 arrays from Lua are affected. Also header enumerator inserted mid-enum renumbers DOUBLE/ENUM/UNKNOWN (only matters for code compiled against the old header and passing the enum across the library boundary; none found in this tree).

luaTableToBuffer INT64/UINT64 cases are wrapped in #ifdef DBF_INT64, but in EPICS Base 7.0.10 dbFldTypes.h DBF_INT64 is an enum member, not a macro, so the branches are compiled out. A waveform/aai with FTVL=INT64 or UINT64 gets NORD set to the table length while the buffer is left unchanged (executed: VAL [0 0 0], NORD 3), a silent wrong value instead of an alarm. Also non-integer floats in an integer-FTVL table become 0 silently (lua_tointeger), and FTVL ENUM and other default types return a count without writing. luaBufferToTable is unused.

scores.note: New int64in/int64out/mbbiDirect/mbboDirect DTYPs (not defect fixes) plus a real lepicslib change: INT64/UINT64 fields now go through a 64-bit path. Probe on the pin: epics.get of an int64in holding 5e9 returns float 5000000000.0, and epics.put(int64out,9000000000) reads back 410065408.0 (32-bit truncation); with F1 both are exact Lua integers. That truncation is a real but narrow bug, and nothing in this tree uses int64 PVs. Shipped luaDtypTest passes with the new mbbiDirect (return 2 path) and int64 cases (472 tests vs 468). Cost: DB_LUA_INT64 is inserted mid-enum in luaEpics.h (installed header; any out-of-tree code compiled against the old header sees shifted DB_LUA_DOUBLE/ENUM/UNKNOWN), luaSupport.dbd gains mbbiDirect/mbboDirect devices, LUA_DEPS gains luaInt64Support.dbd under BASE_7_0, and a regression: epics.get on an INT64 waveform returns nil on F1 (table of doubles on the pin) because db_get's array switch has no DB_LUA_INT64 case. Clean apply on the pin, builds, no other module links lua.

New lsi/lso DTYPs plus a lepicslib change so epics.get/put/PV use the VAL$ char-array view for DBF_STRING fields larger than 40 bytes (lsi/lso/printf); fixes 40-char truncation for those records. devLuaLsi copies bounded by SIZV-1 and NUL-terminates, so no overflow. Requires F1 (luaSupport.dbd, Makefile, luaDtypTest.cpp/.db/.lua context; alone: several hunks FAILED and fuzz). On the chain luaDtypTest lsi/lso and luaEpicsTest long-string round trip pass (chain 489 tests). Minor: dollar-name logic appends '$' to the whole name when the record name contains a dot, which fails dbNameToAddr and silently falls back to truncated access. Behaviour change also hits non-lua lsi/lso/printf users of epics.get/put (improvement). Medium blast radius (shared lepicslib).

New waveform/aai/aao DTYPs with luaTableToBuffer/luaBufferToTable in devUtil. Needs F1 and F2 (dbd, Makefile, test hunks; alone 5+ hunks FAILED). Chain tests pass (waveform double and string, aai int, aao double). Example IOC run confirms waveform fill (NORD=5) and aao read of record.VAL. Reading the code: luaTableToBuffer applies lua_tointeger/lua_tonumber with no type check, so non-numeric or non-integral table values are silently stored as 0; DBF_ENUM/other FTVL are left unchanged but NORD still counts them; luaBufferToTable is exported but unused (dead code; aao relies on existing record.VAL conversion). defects.description: Regression: dbf_to_lua_type now returns DB_LUA_INT64 for INT64/UINT64, but db_get's array switch (lepicslib.cpp) has no DB_LUA_INT64 case, so epics.get('<INT64 waveform>') returns nil on the chain where the pin returns a table of doubles (probe: pin 'table 3 7000000000.0', chain 'nil nil nil'). luascriptRecord.cpp comments still say INT64 maps to DB_LUA_DOUBLE and its switch has no INT64 case; scalar luascript inputs still worked in my probe because they read as double. Also DB_LUA_INT64 inserted in the middle of enum db_lua_type in the installed luaEpics.h shifts values of later enumerators.

luaTableToBuffer does no type check: non-numeric entries or non-integral floats into integer FTVL become 0 silently (lua_tointeger), and unsupported FTVL values leave stale data while NORD still counts them. luaBufferToTable is added and exported but never called (code read only).

longStringDollarName appends '$' to the whole name whenever the name contains a dot, so a record name containing a dot (not a field separator) makes dbNameToAddr fail and the code silently falls back to the 40-char path (code read only).
Comment in st.lua says expected 'sum = 100' but the run printed 'sum = 100.0'. Example needs F1 to F3 or dtyp.db fails to load.

scores.note: Adds int64in/int64out and mbbiDirect/mbboDirect DTYP (4 new dev-support files, new luaInt64Support.dbd, 2 entries in luaSupport.dbd) plus a lepicslib INT64 path. Only one of the four with a real functional fix: on the pin epics.put('int64rec',7000000000) truncates to -1589934592 and epics.get returns a float; with F1 both are exact (my r5Test on pin vs chain). Cost: INT64/UINT64 is now a new db_lua_type (DB_LUA_INT64 inserted mid-enum in luaEpics.h) that two consumers do not handle: db_get array path (INT64 waveform epics.get now returns nil + 'Failed to read local PV (field_type=7, lua_type=3)', pin returned a table) and luascriptRecord loadStrings (INAA link to an INT64 field now ends INVALID/UDF, pin gave a table). UINT64 >= 2^63 now reads as negative integer (pin: 1.8446744073709552e+19). No facility IOC in this repo uses lua, so exposure is only site IOCs. Applies cleanly (no fuzz), builds, shipped tests 468 -> 472 pass. Touches shared lepicslib/luaEpics.h, so locality is middling. Prerequisite for F2 and F3.

Adds lsi/lso DTYP and makes epics.get/put on long-string fields (DBF_STRING with field_size>40) go through the VAL$ char-array view, so 100-char strings are no longer truncated at 40 (luaEpicsTest testLongStringRoundTrip: LEN 101, get returns 100 chars). lsi read copies at most sizv-1 bytes and NUL-terminates: bounded, no OOB seen. Changes lepicslib epics_get/epics_put behaviour for any >40-char string field, but only for fields that were already truncated. Does not apply to the pin alone (Makefile, luaSupport.dbd, luaDtypTest.* hunks fail; lepicslib hunks apply) so a carry needs F1 and inherits its INT64 regression. Chain builds, tests pass.

Adds waveform/aai/aao DTYP with luaTableToBuffer/luaBufferToTable in devUtil.cpp (declared in installed devUtil.h; additive). Read path caps count at NELM before writing, string slots use MAX_STRING_SIZE with explicit NUL: no OOB found by reading. Silent behaviours: non-numeric elements become 0, tables stop at first nil, unsupported FTVL (e.g. ENUM) leaves the buffer untouched but still sets NORD, luaBufferToTable is unused by the devices. Interaction with F1: luaTableToBuffer supports FTVL INT64/UINT64 but epics.get of an INT64 array fails after F1, so an INT64 aao/waveform can be written but not read back by record.VAL. Test aao_sum is never asserted, so testAaoDouble does not prove the callback saw the array. Largest facility feature (Lua-generated waveforms), but a new feature, not a fix. Needs F1+F2 (Makefile, dbd, test context fails on pin alone, 6 files). Chain tests pass (489).

Only iocs/iocLuaExample/iocBoot/08-LuaDTYPSupport files (dtyp.db, scripts/dtyp.lua, st.lua). Applies cleanly to the pin alone (patch -p1 --dry-run rc 0, no fuzz), no library or dbd code, zero runtime risk. But the example loads lsi/lso/waveform/aao with DTYP lua, which exist only with F1-F3, so on the pin the example IOC would fail to load those records; useless as a standalone carry. Example is not built by the default recipe (BUILD_IOCS) and the example IOC link fails on the pin too in my layout, so I only read it; string length claim (55 chars) checked.

defects.description: Regression: DB_LUA_INT64 added but unhandled in db_get array path, so epics.get of an INT64 (and UINT64) array/waveform returns nil, 'Failed to read local PV (field_type=7, lua_type=3)' (pin returned a 4-element table with 5e9 intact). Evidence: r5Test wf64 on pin vs chain.

Regression: luascriptRecord loadStrings switch on dbf_to_lua_type has no DB_LUA_INT64 case, so a luascript INAA..INJJ link to an INT64 field now hits default, linkStatus=-1, record ends SEVR INVALID / STAT UDF (pin: AA table, NO_ALARM). The code comment at luascriptRecord.cpp:643 still says INT64 maps to the double case, now stale.

UINT64 fields map to lua_Integer: values >= 2^63 wrap negative (epics.put -1 then get returns -1; pin returned 1.8446744073709552e+19). Also luaEpics.h inserts DB_LUA_INT64 mid-enum, shifting DOUBLE/ENUM/UNKNOWN values; harmless in-tree (static inline users only) but an ABI change for out-of-tree code built against old headers.

luaTableToBuffer leaves buffer unchanged for unsupported FTVL but the device still sets NORD to count; non-numeric table elements silently store 0. testAaoDouble never asserts aao_sum so the aao callback receiving the array is untested. INT64 FTVL arrays can be written but not read back via record.VAL because of the F1 regression.
